title: U.S. House · Missouri's 8th District
area: Southeast Missouri, the Bootheel and the Ozarks, including Cape Girardeau, Poplar Bluff and West Plains.

context.text: Incumbent Jason Smith won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Gordon Heslop. Christopher Reichard won the Democratic primary over Frank Barnitz. Rebecca Sharpe Lombard advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Jason Smith
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2013); Chairman, House Committee on Ways and Means

priorities.text: Official House issues page organizes his stated priorities around veterans ("American Heroes"), healthcare freedom, agriculture ("Focused on Farms"), deregulation ("Keeping Washington Out of Missouri"), and lower taxes ("Your Money Belongs in Your Pocket").

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Joint Committee on Taxation in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served in the Missouri House of Representatives representing District 120 from 2005 to 2013.

candidates.researchNotes: As Ways and Means chairman, Smith has an extensive legislative record beyond what a basic-tier pass covers; key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Christopher Reichard

priorities.text: Labor: says his primary goal is strengthening the working class by removing restrictions on unions that he says have held them back since 1947 (a reference to the Taft-Hartley Act).
Says he wants to restore federal departments and programs he says were cut, including re-establishing what he calls healthy trade policies.
Says he aims to protect and defend the Constitution and reinforce checks and balances among the branches of government.

positions.summary: His campaign website lists pushing to de-fund and abolish ICE among his goals.
positions.quote: Push to de-fund and abolish ICE

positions.summary: His campaign website lists Medicare-For-All among the bills he says would address healthcare funding problems.
positions.quote: Medicare-For-All and several stepping stone bills to get us there without shocking the system.

positions.summary: His campaign website lists ending private education voucher systems among his education goals.
positions.quote: Ending private education vouchers systems that have been taking resources away from public education.

positions.summary: His campaign website text as reproduced by Ballotpedia (July 22, 2026) states support for access to abortion care; that text was not found on his current issues page.
positions.quote: This includes access to safe abortion care.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his campaign issues page and his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (which reproduces a July 22, 2026 version of the site). No elected office. Not found: stated positions on guns, taxes, housing, climate or other listed issues. A minimum-wage position was removed earlier because his survey answer addresses union strength generally.

statements.quote: Tariffs and soured trade deals added ~$2,400/yr to average family costs

candidates.name: Rebecca Sharpe Lombard
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, or public statements of positions found for Rebecca Sharpe Lombard (checked Ballotpedia, BallotReady, iVoterGuide and a web search, October 2026).
